name: Godié
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 6 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Egner, Inge. 2015. Discourse Features of Godié Narrative. SIL e-Books 65. Dallas: SIL International. 368 pp. (open-access publisher PDF; downloaded via the Internet Archive snapshot of the sil.org file)
catalog_locator: §2.1 Phonology, pp. 4-5; the single 'stress' token is at p. 79 (of the saved)
catalog_quote: Godié is a tonal language with three level tones: high, mid, and low. High tone is represented in the orthography by a straight apostrophe <'> and low tone by a hyphen <-> while mid tone is left unmarked. Lexical tones are written at the beginning of a word in Godié, as shown in example (1). ... Tone plays an important role in Godié grammar (see Gratrix 1975). In Godié orthography, grammatical tones—unlike lexical tones illustrated in example (1) above—are generally written at the end of the word. For example, the oblique marker ‘OBL’ and the negative auxiliary ‘XNEG’ are both realized by a floating high tone. ... For words longer than one syllable (including compound words), the tone of the following syllable or syllables is predictable for a native speaker. Thus there is no need to indicate these tones in the orthography.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

The section goes on to say grammatical (floating) tones are written w…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Godié is a three-level-tone language (H, M, L) with lexical tone on the word and floating grammatical tones; no source opened mentions word stress at all, so no stress placement rule can be stated.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any source opened.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. Zogbo 2019 (p. 726 fn. 2) adds that Godié has 'only remnants of a fourth tone (Gratrix 1975)'. Egner p. 79 remarks that the clause connective ɩyä 'receives more stress than -yä alone' — an emphasis/phrasing observation about one particle, not a word-stress rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level lexical tone (tone written at the beginning of the word) plus word-final grammatical floating tones; description is orthography-based (Jluko and Kagbo dialects underlie SIL work). Corroborated by Hewson & Beaudoin-Lietz 2010 p. 1 ('Godié has three tones, Low, Mid, and High', after Marchese 1986:16) and Godé 2008 preface p. 14 ('trois tons').
new_statements.identity_note: Godié (godi1239) has nine mutually intelligible dialects (Marchese 1983: 37). The SIL materials (Egner 2015; Petit dictionnaire 2004) are based on the Jluko (jluk1238) and Kagbo (kagb1242, the written standard) dialects; Godé/N'Dré 2008, 2016, 2025 describe the Dadjriwalé (dagl1238) dialect of the eastern Godié area; Kokora 1976 'Koyo' = the koyɩwalɩ dialect (koyo1243). WALS keeps Dadjriwalé (ddj) as a separate lect. N'Dré 2025 p. 12 fn. 6 states that Victor Godé and Damanan N'dré are the same author.

tone_statements.citation: N'dré, Damanan. 2016. Rapport ton/consonne et ton bas flottant dans les constructions associatives du dadjriwalé [Tone/consonant relationship and floating low tone in associative constructions of Dadjriwale]. Revue Algérienne des Sciences du Langage (RASDL, ISSN 2507-721X) vol. 1, n° spécial / no. 3: 87-111 (landing page) = pp. 62-83 (PDF pagination). Alger: ASJP/CERIST. Université Alassane Ouattara, Côte d'Ivoire.
tone_statements.quote: Dans les langues kru et plus particulièrement en dadjriwalé, ce phénomène est observé dans les constructions associatives de formants X1+X2. Dans ces constructions, le ton haut de la syllabe finale du mot qui précède (X1) se propage sur la première syllabe du mot qui suit (X2). ... Les consonnes opaques sont des consonnes qui ont le ton bas comme ton sous-jacent. La caractéristique majeure de ce ton bas, c’est de bloquer la propagation d’un ton haut qui précède, sur le ton bas ou moyen qui suit. ... Ces tons haut [H] et moyen [M] sont abaissés d’un cran. Le ton haut [H] devient ton moyen [M] et le ton moyen [M] devient ton bas [B] dans la construction associative.
tone_statements.translation: In the Kru languages and more particularly in Dadjriwalé, this phenomenon [tone spreading] is observed in associative constructions of the form X1+X2. In these constructions the high tone of the final syllable of the preceding word (X1) spreads onto the first syllable of the following word (X2). ... Opaque consonants are consonants that have low tone as their underlying tone. The main property of this low tone is to block the spreading of a preceding high tone onto a following low or mid tone. ... These high [H] and mid [M] tones are lowered by one step. High [H] becomes mid [M] and mid [M] becomes low [L] in the associative construction.
tone_statements.locator: Introduction; §2 'Le rapport ton/consonne'; §3 associative constructions ex. (9) (journal pagination 62-83)
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones H, M, L (B) presupposed; H spreads rightward across a word boundary in associative constructions unless the following consonant is 'opaque' (underlyingly L-bearing: voiced obstruents), a distinction the author finds disintegrating; a floating L tone in associative constructions docks on the final syllable of X1 and the initial syllable of X2, deletes X2's M, and lowers subsequen…

tone_statements.citation: Godé, Gohi Victor (2006). Le «dadjriwalé», un dialecte du godié, langue kru de la Côte d'Ivoire: phonologie, grammaire, lexique. Paris: École des Hautes Études en Sciences Sociales.
tone_statements.quote: Notons, par anticipation, que le dialecte possède six (6) tons phonétiques, dont seulement trois sont phonologiques. … Il s’agit des trois tons ponctuels haut (H), moyen (M) et bas (B), des modulés bas-haut (BH), haut-bas (HB) et haut-moyen(HM). … Dans les limites de notre corpus, nous n’avons pu observer une opposition à valeur distinctive entre tons ponctuels et tons modulés. … Cela veut dire que le dadjriwalé ne connaît pas de ton modulé phonologique.
tone_statements.translation: Let us note in advance that the dialect has six (6) phonetic tones, of which only three are phonological. … These are the three level tones high (H), mid (M) and low (B), and the contours low-high (BH), high-low (HB) and high-mid (HM). … Within the limits of our corpus we could not observe any distinctive opposition between level tones and contour tones. … This means that Dadjriwalé has no phonological contour tone.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 57, 60, 63 (Chapitre 3 'Le système tonal', intro, §1.3 'Tableau récapitulatif des tons phonétiques', §2.1 'Les tons modulés: tons phonétiques'); restated Conclusion générale p. 383
tone_statements.summary: Three contrastive level tones, high, mid, low, on the syllable; surface HL, LH, HM contours are two-tone sequences; low tone marks perfective and, as a floating tone, definiteness; nothing on stress.
